Web-first vs generic assertions: what's the difference?
a: Web-first: actual is a locator/page, needs await, retries until pass or timeout (5 s). Generic: actual is a plain value, no await, checks once. Use web-first for anything on the page.

q: Why is expect(await locator.textContent()).toBe('Complete!') flaky?
a: textContent() reads the text ONCE, maybe before the page updated. Use await expect(locator).toHaveText('Complete!'), which retries.

q: When do you use expect.poll and when toPass?
a: expect.poll: retry a function that RETURNS a value (API, calculation) until a matcher passes. toPass: retry a whole BLOCK of steps/assertions until it stops throwing (always give it a timeout).

q: When is expect.soft a good idea, and when not?
a: Good: many independent checks on one page (you want to see all failures). Not: when the next steps depend on the check (the test would fail later with a confusing error).

q: A web-first assertion without await: what happens?
a: The test does not wait for it. It moves on (or ends) immediately, and the assertion may fail later with a confusing error, or not count at all. Always write await expect(locator)...
